analytics_rules: Map events to verified user journeys and customer-approved goals.
Define event names and success conditions before measurement begins.
Use aggregated counts where individual-level tracking is unnecessary.
Do not collect patient names, health details, test results, or appointment details in generic analytics events.
Avoid sensitive information in URLs, event parameters, session replay, and error logs.
Do not infer clinical outcomes from website engagement.
Check tracking accuracy before interpreting conversion changes.
diagnostic_rules: If a step has unusually high abandonment, investigate usability, errors, performance, and unclear content.
Treat abandonment as a signal to investigate, not proof of a specific cause.
Separate technical failures from intentional exits and unavailable services.
Use user research or approved feedback methods to validate important hypotheses.
Never change a critical healthcare workflow solely to increase conversion.
